results.corrected_title: Year-old AI lab Flapping Airplanes raises $1 billion Series A, reportedly at a $6 billion valuation
results.corrected_summary: On 21 October 2026, Flapping Airplanes announced on its X account a $1 billion Series A co-led by Index and Lux. Bloomberg reported the valuation at about $6 billion, four times the $1.5 billion valuation of its $180 million seed round roughly nine months earlier. The company builds AI models meant to train on much less data, plus a 'megakernel' framework that aims to keep GPUs busy.
key_facts: $1B Series A co-led by Index and Lux, announced 21 Oct 2026 on the company's X account
Valuation of about $6B is reported by Bloomberg; the company has not confirmed it
Previous round: $180M seed about nine months earlier, led by GV, Sequoia and Index, at a $1.5B valuation
Other investors named: Sequoia, GV, Kleiner Perkins, Valor, Atreides, A* and Nvidia
Founders: Aidan Smith, Asher Spector and Ben Spector
results.issues: The $6B valuation comes from a Bloomberg report and the company has not confirmed it. The Bloomberg article itself was not opened. The original's 'reportedly' wording is correct.

results.corrected_title: Trump says new data centres are 'mandated' to make their own power and should pay communities a 'dividend'
results.corrected_summary: In a Truth Social post on 21 October 2026, Trump wrote that new large data centres are 'mandated by me' to generate their own electricity and give or sell any surplus to the local community or grid, saying this could lower power prices. He also urged developers to pay communities a 'dividend' to win local support. He gave no amounts, and it is unclear whether any executive action or enforcement will follow.
key_facts: Posted on Truth Social on Wednesday 21 Oct 2026
Quote: data centres 'mandated by me to make their own electricity and give or sell any excess back to the local community'
Urged developers to pay communities a 'dividend' and wrote 'MAKE DEALS, and get them built!!!'
No dollar amounts or enforcement mechanism; unclear whether executive action will follow
Context: earlier this month, FERC rejected efforts to make data centres on the largest US grid bring their own generation; data-centre power costs are an issue ahead of the November midterms
results.issues: No issues found. The 'mandate' has no formal legal mechanism behind it.

results.corrected_title: DNV foundation awards NOK 96 million to Nordic risk research, including three AI-safety projects
results.corrected_summary: On 22 October 2026, Stiftelsen Det Norske Veritas announced NOK 96 million for 10 research projects in Norway, Denmark, Sweden and Finland, chosen from 145 applications in its first funding call. Three projects, under the autonomous systems theme, deal with AI safety. One is EMERGE at the University of Oslo, led by Malcolm Langford, which studies unexpected behaviour in advanced AI, including what happens when multiple AI agents interact. The other two are at DTU and Aalto University.
key_facts: NOK 96 million to 10 projects at universities in Norway, Denmark, Sweden and Finland
145 applications in the foundation's first funding call

Three AI-safety projects under autonomous systems: EMERGE (University of Oslo, Malcolm Langford), certifiable autonomous AI control of critical infrastructure (DTU, Filipe Rodrigues), PRAXIS (Aalto, Jiancheng Yang)
The other projects cover critical raw materials (mostly NTNU) and societal risks
Research minister Eileen Fugelsnes welcomed the foundation's support for basic research
results.issues: The claims match the source. The only source is DNV's own press release; I found no independent coverage.
